tagline.text: A small coastal city southwest of Cebu City, enjoyed for its boardwalk, church and waterfront walks

location.label: Location
location.text: Southwestern coast of Cebu Island, a city about 21 km southwest of Cebu City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,500 (per person, based on transport and meals, as a day trip from Cebu City)

children.text: Naga City is a coastal city about 21 km southwest of Cebu City, with a boardwalk along the sea, the church of Saint Francis of Assisi and a new park. It makes a quiet urban walk that can be done in half a day from Cebu City.

Naga City is a city on the southwestern coast of Cebu Island, usually called "Naga, Cebu" to tell it apart from the city of the same name in Bicol. It is about 21 km by road from central Cebu City, and the 2024 census counted about 139,000 residents. The name is said to come from the narra trees that once grew widely here. It became a municipality on June 12, 1829, splitting off from San Nicolas; after a plebiscite in 2007 and legal disputes it was confirmed as a city in 2011, and the League of Cities recognized it in 2013.

Naga has a deep industrial history. Coal was found in the uplands of Uling and Lutac in the Spanish period, and in 1921 the government built the country's first cement plant in Tinaan (today's APO Cement Plant). About three-quarters of the town was destroyed in World War II, and the Naga coal plant, which opened in 1981, stopped operating in 2015. As a result, visitors tend to see it less as a glamorous tourist spot and more as the seaside of a working city. This industrial heritage means factory districts and housing mix across the city, and today Naga is growing quickly as a satellite and commuter city of Metro Cebu. Walking the coastal road, you see old harbor neighborhoods beside new apartment blocks, which hints at how the city has changed.

Even so, the seaside promenades are well developed. The main sights are the City of Naga Boardwalk on the shore behind the city plaza, St. Francis Ocean Park and Baywalk, the park Pasilong sa Naga designed by Kenneth Cobonpue and opened in October 2021, the city museum Museo Naga on the second floor of the old municipal hall, and the church of Saint Francis of Assisi, the city's patron saint. It suits a half-day outing: step away from the bustle of Cebu City, walk by the sea at sunset, have a light snack and head back. Sports facilities also stand out. The Teodoro Mendiola Sports Field and Oval, which opened in December 2015, has a track, an 8-lane Olympic-size swimming pool and courts, and hosted the 2016 and 2017 Central Visayas student games. The city also has a lighthouse, a good spot for seaside photos. Whether visitors can use each facility differs, so ask city hall.

The highest point in the city is Mt. Uling in Uling (about 613 m above sea level), and Mt. Naupa is one of Cebu's known trekking spots. In Inoburan there is a mangrove eco-tourism area. However, these natural sights have no consistent opening status or trail information, so ask the city tourism office or a local guide first.

This wooden walkway runs along the shore behind the soccer field of the city plaza. It has benches facing the sea and photo spots, there is no entrance fee, and it is at its best at night once the lights come on after sunset. The midday sun is strong, so go in the early morning or late afternoon.

blocks.title: St. Francis Ocean Park and Baywalk

children.text: This is a walking and resting area along the coast, where many locals jog and exercise morning and evening. Walking it together with the boardwalk makes a full day's stroll.

blocks.title: Church of Saint Francis of Assisi

children.text: This archdiocesan shrine is dedicated to the city's patron saint, Saint Francis. Wikipedia describes it as a Catholic church blending Mudejar style. The city's feast day is
October 10
, and the traditional Easter event "Sugat sa Naga" is also held around here.
Designed by Cebu-born designer Kenneth Cobonpue, this park opened in
October 2021
. It was built on the site of the old municipal park at twice the size, with interlocking rings, winding paths, elevated walkways, fountains and benches.

Located on the second floor of the old municipal hall, the museum introduces the city's history, heritage and environment. When it opened it accepted visits by appointment only, so ask city hall about how and when it opens now.
This is known as a mountain trekking spot in Naga. Sources describe the route and duration differently, so it is safest to go with a local guide or the guidance of the city tourism office.

This mangrove area is listed as an eco-tourism site in the city's tourism information. It suits those who want coastal and tidal-flat scenery and birds, but you should check in advance how visitors are admitted.
At Christmas the "Dagitab Festival of Lights" lights lanterns on the boardwalk, and at Easter there is "Sugat sa Naga." Dates and program change every year.
Take a bus or jeepney to Naga from the Cebu South Bus Terminal or SM City Cebu.
Get off at the Church of Saint Francis of Assisi and look around the church and the city plaza.
See Pasilong sa Naga park and then Museo Naga.
Walk the boardwalk and baywalk and watch the sunset.
Have an evening snack at a restaurant or food stall around the plaza, then head back.
Return transport thins out late at night, so check the last bus and jeepney times in advance.
Set out from your hotel and, in Naga town, get guidance from a local guide or the city tourism office.
Start trekking in the cool of the morning and bring plenty of water.
Come down and have lunch at a restaurant in town.
Relax on the boardwalk to end the day.
There is no confirmed, current official information on the route and duration, so follow your guide's instructions.
Direct flights run daily from Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) and take about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Check airlines and schedules when booking.
You can go from the airport to Naga by taxi or Grab, but the distance is long and costs time and money (check locally). Most people start their itinerary in Cebu City.
The road distance from Cebu City to Naga is about
21 km
, and it usually takes about
45 minutes to 1 hour
, longer depending on traffic.

Take a southbound bus from the South Bus Terminal and tell the conductor you are getting off at the poblacion (town center). Some guides mention a direct bus (KMK) from the SM City Cebu side, but routes and frequency should be confirmed locally. You can also take a jeepney to Naga from in front of the Our Lady of Lourdes shrine in Punta Princesa or Pardo Church, but some cars stop at Minglanilla, so confirm that it goes to Naga.
Southbound buses (from the South Bus Terminal) also pass through Naga. Get off in front of the Church of Saint Francis of Assisi or near the plaza. Check fares locally.
A Grab or taxi from Cebu City is the most convenient, but the fare varies with distance and congestion (check locally).
Return rides can be hard to find late at night, so finish a round trip before dark.
The plaza, church and boardwalk are within walking distance of each other; for outlying sights use a tricycle or motorbike. Check fares locally by section.
Naga has the same tropical climate as Cebu City, and since the visit is mostly on foot, the dry season is best.

In December you can see the lantern decorations on the boardwalk and the Dagitab Festival of Lights, and around Easter Sugat sa Naga is held. Crowds grow in these periods, so make use of daytime hours.

rows: Best for walking; December has the lantern festival

Travelers usually stay in Cebu City or Mactan and visit Naga as a half-day or one-day trip. There are small lodgings in Naga itself, but the choice is limited, so check the latest reviews on a booking site. Unless you plan an early-morning climb of Mt. Naupa, there is little need to stay.

Food centers on bakeries, restaurants, Cebuano eateries, grilled chicken and pork belly restaurants, and street stalls around the plaza. Near the boardwalk there are street food and snack shops, and Jollibee and Chowking are within walking distance. No specialty dish has been confirmed, so think of it as a light taste of Cebuano grilled food and seafood. The plaza is quiet at midday and people gather at the boardwalk from sunset on, so timing your meal for sunset gives the best feel of local life. Bring enough cash and ask the price first at stalls.
The
Cebu park guide
lists Pasilong sa Naga as a free public space. Early mornings and late afternoons are more comfortable for combining it with the boardwalk. Event hours may differ.
Always ask the driver whether the bus or jeepney goes all the way to Naga. Some end at Minglanilla.
Combining the church and the boardwalk on foot near the plaza takes almost no travel time.
Return transport thins out late at night, so plan to be back before dark.
Dress with your shoulders and knees covered when visiting the church.
Ask the city tourism office or a local guide first about Mt. Naupa or the mangroves.
Opening hours of Museo Naga and the park can change, so check city hall announcements before visiting.
There are congested stretches between Cebu City and Naga, so leave early for an afternoon trip and plan to return after the evening rush.
It is not certain that the Naga lighthouse and sports facilities are open to the general public, so treat them as photo stops and ask city hall before visiting.
Wooden boardwalk floors can be slippery right after rain, so wear sandals or sneakers with good grip, and do not stand close to the water when waves are breaking.
Official up-to-date guidance on trekking and outlying natural sights is lacking. Do not go alone; check with a local guide or the city tourism office first.
Naga shares its name with Naga City in Bicol. On a map app, be sure to search for "Naga, Cebu."
Some buses and jeepneys end at Minglanilla, so confirm the destination.
The boardwalk gets crowded at night but has dark stretches, so watch your valuables and go with companions.
Fares and opening hours change often, and this guide covers what could be confirmed as of 2026. Check the latest announcements.
About
21 km
to the northeast, the central city of Cebu; in
Cebu City
you can see the Basilica del Santo Niño and Magellan's Cross together.
Carcar
, a historic town to the south, is known for old buildings and snacks, and pairs well with Naga as a one-day outing.
At
Carbon Market
, the old market of Cebu City, you can see Cebuano snacks and market scenes, a good stop before or after heading to Naga.
